newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn firm in nearbys on exports, quiet day.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn firm in nearbys on exports, quiet day.

text.p: CBOT corn futures were firm in the nearby months with support from USDA's weekly export inspections report, but trading was quiet before the release Wednesday of USDA's February supply/demand report, traders said.
USDA Monday said U.S. corn inspected for export during the week ended February 6 totaled 45.080 million bushels, above expectations for 33 to 36 million bushels.
Traders also said slow farmer selling helped underpin the nearby contracts.
The market was preparing for Wednesday's supply/demand report.

Analysts Friday said a recent pickup in the U.S. corn export pace may not be enought to prevent the U.S. Department of Agriculture from cutting its estimate for 1996-97 when it issues its supply/demand report. Dean Witter analyst Jerry Gidel said Friday he expected USDA to cut its estimate of corn exports in 1996-97 (September/August) by 50 to 75 million bushels, prompting a hike in ending stocks.
At 1123 CST, corn was 1/2 cent per bushel higher to 3/4 lower, with March up 1/2 at $2.71-1/2.
Chartists early Monday cited first resistance in March corn at $2.72-3/4 and second resistance at $2.76-3/4. The session high for March as of 1125 CST was $2.72.
First support for March was $2.68-3/4 and second support was $2.64-3/4. The session low for March as of 1127 CST, was $2.70-3/4.

As of 1130 CST, the nine-day relative strength index (RSI) for March was near neutral territory at 53 percent. The trade generally considers an RSI of 30 or less as an oversold market and 70 or more as an overbought market.

Farmers Commodities Corp bought one-half million bushels of March as did Iowa Grain, traders said. ADM Investor Services sold 1.5 million bushels of March and SAK Futures sold one-half million bushels of March, traders said.
